new.md:
Create a new `GtkEntryBuffer` object.

Optionally, specify initial text to set in the buffer.

doc.brief: Holds the text that is displayed in a single-line text entry widget.
doc.md:
Holds the text that is displayed in a single-line text entry widget.

A single `GtkEntryBuffer` object can be shared by multiple widgets
which will then share the same text content, but not the cursor
position, visibility attributes, icon etc.

`GtkEntryBuffer` may be derived from. Such a derived class might allow
text to be stored in an alternate location, such as non-pageable memory,
useful in the case of important passwords. Or a derived class could
integrate with an application’s concept of undo/redo.

delete_text.brief: Deletes a sequence of characters from the buffer.
delete_text.md:
Deletes a sequence of characters from the buffer.

`n_chars` characters are deleted starting at `position`.
If `n_chars` is negative, then all characters until the
end of the text are deleted.

If `position` or `n_chars` are out of bounds, then they
are coerced to sane values.

Note that the positions are specified in characters,
not bytes.

get_bytes.brief: Retrieves the length in bytes of the buffer.
get_bytes.md:
Retrieves the length in bytes of the buffer.

See [`EntryBuffer.get_length()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.EntryBuffer#method:get_length).

get_length.brief: Retrieves the length in characters of the buffer.
get_length.md: Retrieves the length in characters of the buffer.

get_max_length.brief: Retrieves the maximum allowed length of the text in `buffer`.
get_max_length.md: Retrieves the maximum allowed length of the text in `buffer`.

get_text.brief: Retrieves the contents of the buffer.
get_text.md:
Retrieves the contents of the buffer.

The memory pointer returned by this call will not change
unless this object emits a signal, or is finalized.

insert_text.brief: Inserts `n_chars` characters of `chars` into the contents of the buffer, at position `position`.
insert_text.md:
Inserts `n_chars` characters of `chars` into the contents of the
buffer, at position `position`.

If `n_chars` is negative, then characters from chars will be inserted
until a null-terminator is found. If `position` or `n_chars` are out of
bounds, or the maximum buffer text length is exceeded, then they are
coerced to sane values.

Note that the position and length are in characters, not in bytes.

set_max_length.brief: Sets the maximum allowed length of the contents of the buffer.
set_max_length.md:
Sets the maximum allowed length of the contents of the buffer.

If the current contents are longer than the given length, then
they will be truncated to fit.

set_text.brief: Sets the text in the buffer.
set_text.md:
Sets the text in the buffer.

This is roughly equivalent to calling
[`EntryBuffer.delete_text()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.EntryBuffer#method:delete_text) and
[`EntryBuffer.insert_text()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.EntryBuffer#method:insert_text).

Note that `n_chars` is in characters, not in bytes.

length.brief: The length (in characters) of the text in buffer.
length.md: The length (in characters) of the text in buffer.

max-length.brief: The maximum length (in characters) of the text in the buffer.
max-length.md: The maximum length (in characters) of the text in the buffer.

deleted-text.brief: The text is altered in the default handler for this signal.
deleted-text.md:
The text is altered in the default handler for this signal.

If you want access to the text after the text has been modified,
use %G_CONNECT_AFTER.

inserted-text.brief: This signal is emitted after text is inserted into the buffer.
inserted-text.md: This signal is emitted after text is inserted into the buffer.
